purpose: Define the minimum planning and safety rules a future Patch Planner Agent must follow before proposing or preparing sprint patches for PILAR.
non_goals: No prompt or i18n source changes in this sprint

rules.title: Sprint plan must use the PILAR sprint format
rules.requirement: Every proposed sprint must include Sprint name, goal, scope, files, risk, test and rollback sections before any patch is prepared.

rules.title: Keep one file group per sprint
rules.requirement: Do not mix unrelated file groups such as UI, prompts, report rendering, database and QA in the same sprint.
forbidden_patterns: UI + prompts + PDF + Word + database in one sprint

rules.title: Do not start a new sprint while core gates are red
rules.requirement: If TypeScript, agent:all or relevant validators fail, the Patch Planner must propose a fix, not a new sprint.
forbidden_patterns: Start next sprint despite failed tsc
Start next sprint despite failed agent:all

rules.title: Audit the real file state before patching reused files
rules.requirement: When a file has been patched recently or a previous patch did not apply, collect grep or sed output before preparing another patch.

rules.title: Use downloadable artifacts for Git Bash workflow
rules.requirement: For non-trivial code or docs changes, prepare a downloadable ZIP, patch or Node script instead of long Git Bash heredocs.

rules.title: Never use broad regex replacement over TSX
rules.requirement: TSX and JSX changes must use exact blocks, structured changes or helper additions. Broad replacements across JSX are forbidden.
required_evidence: Exact target block or stable ASCII anchor

rules.title: Patch scripts must back up changed files
rules.requirement: Any script that writes to existing tracked files must create a backup under .patch-backup/sprint-XX before writing.

rules.title: Patch scripts must report outcomes
rules.requirement: Patch scripts must print PATCHED, OK, SKIPPED or FAILED lines so the operator can see exactly what happened.

rules.title: Critical patch anchors must fail closed
rules.requirement: If a critical expected block or anchor is not found, the patch script must exit non-zero and not claim success.
forbidden_patterns: claim success when no diff occurred

rules.title: Preserve Norwegian and international language modes
rules.requirement: Any i18n-related sprint must explicitly preserve Norwegian mode while using English shell labels for non-Norwegian profiles.
forbidden_patterns: locale used as displayLanguage in international context

rules.title: Do not invent AISC or standards table values
rules.requirement: International/AISC changes must not introduce unverified section properties, code constants or final compliance claims.
forbidden_patterns: final AISC compliance without verified data

rules.title: Separate generated artifacts from source changes
rules.requirement: Generated files such as latest health or coverage reports must only be committed when intentionally refreshed.
required_evidence: Generated artifact listed as intentional or restored

rules.title: Stage only files owned by the sprint
rules.requirement: When Claude or another process has parallel changes, only stage the exact files belonging to the current sprint.

rules.title: Verify with TypeScript and relevant gates
rules.requirement: Every code/script sprint must run TypeScript and relevant validators before commit. Runtime/UI changes also require build and manual/runtime tests.
forbidden_patterns: use old DB output as proof for prompt changes

rules.title: Patch Planner remains human-approved
rules.requirement: Patch Planner may propose plans and artifacts, but must not auto-merge, auto-deploy or edit production prompts without explicit human command and review.
